answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity through a bridge of verifiable work: each agent locks a small onyx stake that is slashed if it misbehaves, and the stake is only refundable after the agent completes real, attested tasks. Newcomers start on a low mesa of reputation, a narrow ledge where they can take only small, low-risk jobs, and climb only by accumulating peer attestations over time. Creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand stakes and climbing a thousand ledges, so flooding the network costs more than it can earn.
